title: Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters (Estate Agents and Developers) Bill
what_it_is: Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters (Estate Agents and Developers) Bill

sections.label: Bill's penalty and FATF aims
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to strengthen penalty frameworks, align the regulatory regime with FATF standards, and make miscellaneous amendments on restrictions against convicted persons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Specifically, this Bill seeks to: (a) strengthen current penalty frameworks; (b) further align our regulatory regime with FATF standards; and (c) make miscellaneous amendments to clarify restrictions against convicted persons.

sections.label: $3 billion money laundering case
sections.summary: In the recent $3 billion money laundering case, properties seized from the 10 convicted offenders were estimated at more than $370 million.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the recent $3 billion money laundering case, the total estimated value of properties seized was more than $370 million from the 10 convicted offenders.

sections.label: Estate Agents Act financial penalties
sections.summary: Clauses 8 and 9 amend the Estate Agents Act to impose maximum financial penalties on a per contravention basis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To ensure that our penalty frameworks are sufficiently deterrent, clauses 8 and 9 of the Bill will amend the Estate Agents Act to impose maximum financial penalties on a per contravention basis.

sections.label: Composition sums for developers
sections.summary: Clause 13 raises the HDCLA maximum composition sum to 50% of the maximum fine, and clause 16 allows compounding of SCPA offences by commercial and industrial developers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To strengthen deterrence, clause 13 of the Bill amends the HDCLA to increase the maximum composition sum for housing developers from $5,000, to 50% of the maximum fine prescribed for the offence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 16 of the Bill will also amend the Sale of Commercial Properties Act (SCPA) to allow offences by commercial and industrial developers to be compounded.

sections.label: Due diligence on unrepresented counterparties
sections.summary: Clause 6 amends the Estate Agents Act to require estate agents and salespersons to conduct due diligence on unrepresented counterparties of property transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To align with FATF standards, clause 6 of the Bill amends the Estate Agents Act to require estate agents and salespersons to conduct due diligence measures on such unrepresented counterparties of property transactions.

sections.label: Developers' targeted financial sanctions
sections.summary: Clauses 14 and 17 amend the HDCLA and SCPA to require developers to perform prescribed measures on targeted financial sanctions for terrorism financing and proliferation financing, in addition to terrorism.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In the same vein, clauses 14 and 17 of the Bill amend the HDCLA and SCPA respectively to require developers to perform prescribed measures related to targeted financial sanctions for terrorism financing and proliferation financing, in addition to terrorism.

sections.label: Convicted persons unfit for licences
sections.summary: Clause 2 states that persons convicted of money laundering, terrorism financing or proliferation financing offences are not fit and proper to hold an estate agent licence or salesperson registration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Clause 2 of the Bill clarifies that persons who have been convicted of money laundering, terrorism financing, or proliferation financing offences, whether committed in Singapore or overseas, are not deemed fit and proper to hold an estate agent licence, or a salesperson registration under the Estate Agents Act, given the seriousness of such offences.

sections.label: Higher penalties for property agents
sections.summary: The legislation imposes higher penalties and due diligence obligations on the 36,058 registered property agents for failing to check clients or counterparties where they suspect financial crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Real estate agents, though, are a diverse group and typically self-employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are currently 36,058 registered property agents according to a report in January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The legislation now imposes on them higher penalties and obligations for the failure to do due diligence on either clients or counterparties where they have reason to suspect money laundering, proliferation financing or terrorism financing, where earlier due diligence exercises give them reason to doubt the veracity of the information provided to them.

sections.label: Clarifying framework shortcomings
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify whether the existing framework had shortcomings requiring expanded due diligence obligations on real estate agents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, I will be grateful if the Minister can clarify whether the existing framework has had any shortcomings such that the due diligence obligations imposed on real estate agents have to be expanded.

sections.label: Clarifying additional mischief addressed
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify the additional mischief the legislation intends to capture, noting the Fujian Gang parked three billion in illicit funds in property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Of course, if there is greater mischief that needs to be addressed, then I think this legislation would be fair.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would be grateful for the Minister to clarify the additional mischief that is intended to be captured by this legislation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Improving the regulatory framework is critical, not least because the so-called Fujian Gang had parked a significant amount of their three billion in illicit funds in property.

sections.label: Penalties, scrutiny and maximum fine
sections.summary: The changes apply penalties to each instance of contravention, require more scrutiny of unrepresented counterparties, and raise the maximum penalty from $100,000 to $200,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Changing penalties to each instance of contravention, adding a requirement that unrepresented counterparties in real estate transactions be subject to more scrutiny and raising the maximum penalty from $100,000 to $200,000.

sections.label: Due diligence checks and AML robustness
sections.summary: The Minister for National Development said property agencies and agents must perform due diligence checks on clients, yet some in the sector feel AML procedures are less robust than in finance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to a Parliamentary Question posed by my hon friend Mr Leong Mun Wai, the Minister for National Development indicated that, and I quote, "property agencies and property agents are required to perform due diligence checks on their clients before commencing business, any business relationship or facilitating transaction with them." Yet, in our conversations with those working in the sector, some have raised a nagging sense that AML procedures in the industry are somehow not as robust as those for the financial sector more generally.

sections.label: Money laundering real estate enforcement
sections.summary: This Bill introduces tougher penalties and record-keeping obligations for estate agents and developers to detect and report suspicious transactions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What I feel is more important is a steely eye focus on ensuring enforcement and compliance, for which I hope the Government would redouble the efforts to stamp out the scourge of Singapore-washing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore’s battle against money launderers now moves to the real estate and property sector as we strive to uphold our nation’s financial integrity and a strong reputation as a global financial hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces tougher penalties and record-keeping obligations to ensure that estate agents and developers are better equipped to detect and report suspicious transactions.

sections.label: Stronger investigative powers, two-year timeline
sections.summary: CEA and housing authorities gain stronger investigative powers and broader compliance authority, with a two-year implementation timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specifically, institutions such as the CEA and the relevant housing authorities will gain stronger investigative powers and broader authority to enforce compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The two-year implementation timeline is also very prudent.

sections.label: Compliance support for smaller firms
sections.summary: Smaller firms may struggle with added compliance requirements, prompting a question on scaled measures or support for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: Four, given the additional compliance requirements, smaller firms may face challenges in adapting to this new setup.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: It would be helpful to know if there are any scaled compliance measures for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) or support initiatives such as training, grants, or digital tools to help them meet these obligations without compromising their competitiveness.

sections.label: Three billion dollar laundering incident
sections.summary: Existing real estate money laundering rules exist, but a $3 billion incident last year necessitated this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There are already clear regulations and detailed guidelines against money laundering in our real estate sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the $3 billion money laundering incident last year showed the need for more controls and necessitated the introduction of this Bill.

sections.label: Guidelines and roll-out timeline questions
sections.summary: Questions ask what guidelines estate agents will get to identify suspicious activities and the roll-out timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What specific guidelines will be provided to estate agents to accurately identify suspicious activities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the planned timeline for the roll-out of the new measures?

sections.label: Penalties and enforcement balance questions
sections.summary: Questions ask what penalties apply for non-compliance and how enforcement will avoid overburdening legitimate businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What penalties will be imposed for non-compliance and how will enforcement be balanced to avoid overburdening legitimate businesses?

sections.label: Burden on small estate agencies
sections.summary: The amendments may create an unintended burden on small estate agencies and independent agents, which operate on tight margins and lack resources of larger firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, the amendments may create an unintended burden on small estate agencies and independent agents, which operate on tight margins and often lack the resources of larger firms.

sections.label: Help for smaller agencies compliance
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government plans to help smaller agencies and independent agents meet new compliance requirements without excessive costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, regarding clause 6, section 44BA, how does the Government plan to help smaller agencies and independent agents meet these new compliance requirements without incurring excessive costs?

sections.label: CEA manpower for money laundering
sections.summary: The passage asks whether CEA has the manpower and specialised expertise to detect sophisticated money laundering schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To this end, does CEA currently possess the necessary manpower and specialised expertise to effectively detect sophisticated money laundering schemes, given their complexity and evolving nature?

sections.label: 2023 money laundering case
sections.summary: The 2023 money laundering case involved $3 billion in assets and shows the scale and sophistication of these activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The 2023 money laundering case, involving $3 billion in assets, stands as a stark reminder of the scale and sophistication of these activities.

sections.label: Due diligence on unrepresented counterparties
sections.summary: The Bill requires estate agents and salespersons to conduct due diligence on unrepresented counterparties so both parties face robust checks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Through this Bill, we are requiring estate agents and salespersons to conduct due diligence measures on unrepresented counterparties, so that both parties in a property transaction are subject to robust checks.

sections.label: Proliferation financing screening requirements
sections.summary: The amendments require estate agents, salespersons and developers to screen parties for proliferation financing risks against designated or sanction lists.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The amendments to include proliferation financing will make clear that estate agents, salespersons and developers would also have to screen the necessary parties for proliferation financing risks against relevant designated or sanction lists, which they have already been doing as part of countering terrorism financing.

sections.label: Mandatory AML CPD courses
sections.summary: Anti-money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing CPD courses will be mandatory in the next cycle, with annual training raised to 16 hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For the next continuing professional development cycle, anti-money laundering, countering terrorism financing and countering proliferation financing continuing professional development courses will be made mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This is part of our earlier announced initiative to enhance the continuing professional development framework for the real estate agency industry, by increasing the annual continuing professional development training requirement to 16 hours from the end of this year.

sections.label: Failed due diligence stops transactions
sections.summary: If customer due diligence cannot be completed, the estate agent, salesperson or developer cannot proceed and must assess whether to file a Suspicious Transaction Report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If an estate agent, salesperson or developer is unable to complete the required customer due diligence measures, the estate agent, salesperson or developer cannot proceed with the transaction and must also assess whether a Suspicious Transaction Report should be filed to the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office.

sections.label: Bill implementation timeline June 2025
sections.summary: The Bill will be brought into force in June 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On Mr Don Wee's and Mr Neil Parekh's clarifications on this Bill’s implementation timeline, we will bring it into force in June 2025.

sections.label: Inter-agency taskforce on money laundering
sections.summary: An inter-agency taskforce has been expanded to include all agencies combatting money laundering, including CEA and URA, and a new data-sharing interface is being developed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Today, we already have an inter-agency taskforce to deal with money laundering cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have reinforced this taskforce by expanding its membership to include all agencies involved in combatting money laundering, including CEA and URA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This will strengthen inter-agency coordination for supervisory and enforcement action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are also developing a new interface to facilitate data-sharing across Government agencies so that we will have a more comprehensive picture of potential money laundering risks.

sections.label: Enforcement recommendations and Bill scope
sections.summary: The Inter-Ministerial Committee report recommended strengthening sense-making, information-sharing, legislative levers and reviewing penalty frameworks, and this Act implements one small section of that work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under enforcement, it was recommended that we do a few things, one of which was to strengthen sense-making and information-sharing, and also to enhance legislative levers for law enforcement agencies and then also to continuously review penalty frameworks to ensure they remain proportionate and dissuasive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in other words, the Inter-Ministerial Committee report contain the whole slew of things under those three broad categories; and under the third one, enforcement, there were various things, one of which was to really review the penalty framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, this Act implements one small section of what was a very large body of work with extensive recommendations to strengthen our regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in conclusion, Mr Deputy Speaker, I thank hon Members who have spoken and supported this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This Bill is part of our continuing efforts to bolster our ability to detect and deter money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing within the real estate sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This ensures that our financial and business ecosystem remains reputable and trusted, and continues to thrive.

sections.label: Detect versus enforce provisions
sections.summary: The Bill is primarily concerned with the enforce category, which applies after catching, while detecting earlier is a detect provision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Because in order to catch them earlier, that is a "detect" provision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This Bill is primarily concerned with the "enforce" category.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, you enforce only after you have caught.

sections.label: Early detection recalled
sections.summary: The detection was done quite early, if Members recall.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The detection was actually done quite early, if Members recall.
